answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. Because the plume hash is checked against the onyx checkpoint at intake, the island audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 131 aliases cost 75 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
